newsitem.title: USA: Corporate Express sees Q4 below estimates.
newsitem.headline: Corporate Express sees Q4 below estimates.

text.p: Corporate Express Inc said Wednesday its fourth quarter earnings will be below analysts estimates and that 1996 earnings per share before expenses will be $0.05 to $0.07 below First Call estimates.
Wall Street had been expecting earnings of $0.16 per share for the fourth quarter and $0.50 for the year, according to First Call consensus estimates of the company.
The company said it expects revenue of about $3.2 billion for the fiscal year ended March 1, 1997.

It attributed the expected earnings shortfall to weakness in the operating performance of its same-day delivery business, including the integration of the recently acquired United TransNet Inc UT.N and consolidation of delivery services.
It said previously announced operating expense increases may also have "a short term negative effect."
The company said merger charges for the fourth quarter relating to poolings with Hermann Marketing Inc and Sofco -Mead Inc will be about $7 million.
The Broomfield, Colorado-based company said however that its core business continues to perform above company expectations and that its year-to-year earnings per share should grow.

"We are pleased with our overall trends," the company said in a release. "We expect earnings per share year-to-year to grow approximately 40 percent from the earnings that we expect to report for the fiscal year just ended."
